title: 3D Printing
desc: Learn to design, slice, print, finish and cost 3D-printed parts safely and sell them honestly.
outcomes: Prepare a model and slice it.
Print and finish a useful part.
task: Design or select a part, print it, finish it, test it against a requirement and cost it for sale.
condition: Access to a printer (own, makerspace or partner), a computer, free software, two peers and a mentor.
standard: Part meets the dimensions within 0.3 mm; print log shows settings; failure analysis written; safety rules followed; cost per part shown; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Makers, students, product designers, small manufacturers.
evidence: model, slicer settings, print log, test record, cost sheet

ladder: Printers and materials

L1: learner can name printer types. Focus module: Printers and materials (Understand, 3 h). Pick the printer and material to match the part. Key points: Filament printers melt plastic and lay it in layers; resin printers cure liquid with light. PLA is easy and stiff; PETG is tougher; ABS resists heat but fumes need ventilation; resins give fine detail but need care. Match material to heat, strength and food-contact needs. Check manufacturer guidance.

Teach: open with the worked example. A bracket for a shelf is printed in PETG for toughness; a jewellery prototype is printed in resin for detail. Then set the activity: Compare four materials in a table. Mark against the standard: Table covers strength, heat and ease. Check at this level: Easy filament? Model answer: PLA.
Design for printing

L2: learner knows safety. Focus module: Design for printing (Apply, 4 h). A model designed for printing prints well. Key points: Wall thickness at least two nozzle widths. Avoid steep overhangs or add supports. Orientation affects strength; layers are weak in tension. Allow tolerances of 0.2 to 0.4 mm for fits.

Teach: open with the worked example. A bracket printed on its side is stronger because layer lines run along the load. Then set the activity: Design or choose a part and list its dimensions and orientation. Mark against the standard: Dimensions listed. Check at this level: Overhang fix? Model answer: Supports.
Slicing

L3: learner can slice. Focus module: Slicing (Apply, 4 h). The slicer turns a model into instructions. Key points: Layer height, infill, speed, temperature and supports. Preview the path before printing. Save profiles for materials. Check the first layer.

Teach: open with the worked example. A part is sliced at 0.2 mm layers with 20 per cent infill and 3 walls, printing in 2.5 hours. Then set the activity: Slice your part and record settings. Mark against the standard: Preview checked. Check at this level: Resin safety? Model answer: Gloves and eye protection.
Printing and safety

L4: learner can print. Focus module: Printing and safety (Apply, 4 h). Hot, moving and fumes. Key points: Ventilation and a stable surface. Do not touch hot parts; keep hair and clothes clear. Do not leave long prints unattended without safeguards. Resin: gloves, eye protection and proper waste disposal.

Teach: open with the worked example. A smoke alarm and a fire blanket are kept near the printer. Then set the activity: Print and log. Mark against the standard: Log complete. Check at this level: Why ventilate? Model answer: Fumes.
Troubleshooting

L5: learner can fix and cost. Focus module: Troubleshooting (Analyse, 3 h). Failures teach. Key points: Warping, stringing, poor adhesion and clogs. Change one setting at a time. Keep notes. Maintain the machine.

Teach: open with the worked example. A heated bed and a brim fix warping on a large flat part. Then set the activity: Fix two issues. Mark against the standard: Notes recorded. Check at this level: Warping fix? Model answer: Heated bed.
Testing the part

L6: learner can lead a lab. Focus module: Testing the part (Evaluate, 3 h). Does it meet the requirement? Key points: Dimension check with calipers. Load test within safe limits. Document the results. Retest after changes.

Teach: open with the worked example. A bracket holds 5 kg for 10 minutes without deflection. Then set the activity: Test and record. Mark against the standard: Record complete. Check at this level: Measuring tool? Model answer: Calipers.
Cost and sale

L7: learner can audit. Focus module: Cost and sale (Create, 3 h). Price honestly. Key points: Material, power, machine time, labour and failures. Quote per part. Disclose limits and intended use. Respect intellectual property.

Teach: open with the worked example. Cost 62 INR; price 150 INR. Then set the activity: Cost one part. Mark against the standard: Currency shown. Check at this level: Costs? Model answer: Material, power, time, labour, failures.
